question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{2}+9}{8{x}^{5}+x} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{9}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{8{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{9}{{x}^{5}})}{(8+\frac{1}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{0+0}{8+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
